title: Impact of Obesity Diagnosis on Medication Use

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will use a Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) around the BMI cutoff for obesity. The idea is to exploit the discontinuity in the probability of receiving an obesity diagnosis at the BMI cutoff to identify its causal effect on medication use. The key assumption is that individuals just below and just above the BMI cutoff are comparable except for the treatment assignment determined by crossing the cutoff.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Load the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s100_data.csv")

# Run RDD
rdd_results <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                        x = data$running_var, 
                        c = 0.5, 
                        p = 1, 
                        kernel = "uniform",
                        h = 0.1)

# Print main results
print(rdd_results)

# Conduct robustness check with different bandwidth
rdd_results_robust <- rdrobust(y = data$y, 
                               x = data$running_var, 
                               c = 0.5, 
                               p = 1, 
                               kernel = "uniform",
                               h = 0.2)

# Print robustness results
print(rdd_results_robust)

# Plot the results to visualize the discontinuity
ggplot(data, aes(x = running_var, y = y)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  xlim(0.3, 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "RDD Plot: Impact of Obesity Diagnosis on Medication Use",
       x = "BMI (running variable)",
       y = "Log Medication Use")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect a positive sign on the coefficient measuring the impact of the obesity diagnosis on medication use, indicating that being diagnosed as obese likely increases subsequent medication use. The magnitude will depend on the elasticity of medication use with respect to the diagnosis, but based on typical health responses, an increase in medication use could be between 5-15% in log terms, corresponding to semi-elasticities commonly found in health behavior studies.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare medication use for individuals just above and below the BMI cutoff.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Receiving an obesity diagnosis at the BMI cutoff leads to increased medication use.
